content.text: No arbitration clause exists anywhere; the only forum provision is the New York clause in the General Provisions.

input.quote: the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A.
input.rationale: Governing law is the internal laws of the State of New York (p0145), and disputes must be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the SDNY or any New York State court, plus waivers of venue and forum non conveniens objections (p0146). There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document, so the walk-away risk of an offshore seat does not arise. This sits at the preferred position: New York law and exclusive New York state and federal courts. The only shortfall is cosmetic — venue is fixed to the City of New York rather than New York County specifically, and there is no express temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out (a permitted, not required, feature) — which we note but do not redline.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
mappings.quote: the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: any legal suit, action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement must be instituted in the City of New York, State of New York, and the parties each (i) irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, or any court of the State of New York
